props.title: Good Morning, Night

sections.content: Good Morning, Night represents Marco Bellocchio's masterful examination of Italy's darkest political moment - the 1978 kidnapping and murder of former Prime Minister Aldo Moro by the Red Brigades. Unlike straightforward political thrillers like Il Divo (2008) or The Day of the Jackal (1973), Bellocchio creates a dreamlike psychological study focused on Chiara, a young terrorist struggling with her role in the kidnapping. The film's claustrophobic apartment setting and surreal sequences echo the intimate political tensions of The Conformist (1970).

sections.content: The film's unique power comes from its intimate perspective on political violence. Unlike the broader historical scope of The Battle of Algiers (1966) or the action-driven narrative of Munich (2005), Bellocchio keeps us confined with the kidnappers, forcing us to confront their humanity and contradictions. The surreal dream sequences where Chiara imagines freeing Moro create a haunting contrast with the brutal reality, reminiscent of how United Red Army (2007) explored the psychological toll of radical politics.

Bellocchio's approach to historical events through personal perspective influenced later political films like Carlos (2010) and Uli Edel's The Baader Meinhof Complex (2008). His use of archival footage blended with fictional narrative created a template for examining political trauma that echoes in works like The Lost Honor of Katharina Blum (1975). movies.title: The State I Am In
movies.slug: A teenage girl struggles with her identity as her terrorist parents live underground

sections.content: The film's focus on domestic spaces and daily routines amid political violence creates an unsettling intimacy that influenced later works like In the Name of the Father (1993) and Michael Collins (1996). Bellocchio's decision to tell the story through Chiara's perspective allows examination of how political ideologies affect personal relationships, similar to how The Secret in Their Eyes (2009) used personal narrative to explore state violence.
